job.title: Regional Facilities and Maintenance Engineer
job.description:
Regional Engineering and Facilities Manager
Take ownership. Drive performance. Shape the future.
Are you an ambitious, technically minded and results-driven Engineering and Facilities Manager who thrives on responsibility and enjoys making things happen?
We're looking for an experienced Regional Engineering and Facilities Manager to take ownership of the engineering, maintenance and facilities strategy across a number of temperature-controlled warehouse sites.
This is an exciting opportunity for someone who combines strong technical expertise with commercial awareness, strategic thinking and genuine leadership ability. You'll play a key role in ensuring our facilities operate safely, reliably and efficiently, while identifying opportunities to improve performance, embrace new technology and support the continued growth of the business.
We're looking for someone who doesn't simply maintain the status quo. Someone who challenges existing practices, takes ownership of problems and has the drive and ambition to make a real difference.
Why this opportunity?
Make your mark - Take ownership of a critical regional function, influencing engineering standards, investment decisions and the future development of multiple facilities.
Think beyond engineering - Work alongside senior leadership and operational teams, gaining exposure to a wider European organisation and contributing to strategic business initiatives.
Work in an essential industry - Help maintain the infrastructure that keeps critical food and pharmaceutical supply chains moving.
Drive improvements - Lead projects, modernise systems, introduce smarter maintenance practices and improve efficiency, reliability and sustainability.
Take ownership - Enjoy the autonomy to make decisions, develop your teams and deliver meaningful results across the region.
What will you be doing?
As Regional Engineering and Facilities Manager, you'll be responsible for the performance, reliability and continuous improvement of engineering and facilities across multiple cold storage warehouse locations.
You'll combine technical expertise with a strategic approach, ensuring critical equipment, refrigeration systems and building infrastructure support demanding 24/7 operations.
You'll:
· Take ownership of engineering and facilities across multiple sites, ensuring buildings, refrigeration systems, utilities and equipment operate reliably and efficiently.
· Lead, develop and motivate engineering teams, building a culture of accountability, technical capability and high performance.
· Drive preventative and predictive maintenance programmes to minimise breakdowns, reduce downtime and maximise asset reliability.
· Oversee refrigeration infrastructure, including ammonia, CO2 and Freon-based systems, ensuring the highest standards of maintenance and operational control.
· Lead engineering projects, equipment upgrades and facility improvements, managing capital investment and maintenance budgets to deliver results within agreed timescales and costs.
· Ensure facilities meet all relevant health, safety, environmental and cold-chain compliance requirements, maintaining a proactive approach to audits and risk management.
· Manage contractors, suppliers and service providers, negotiating agreements, monitoring performance and ensuring value for money.
· Use engineering KPIs, CMMS and monitoring systems to identify opportunities for improvement, increase equipment uptime and modernise maintenance practices.
· Drive energy efficiency, sustainability and technology initiatives, supporting the organisation's wider growth and decarbonisation objectives.
· Work closely with operational teams, senior management and Group Engineering to align priorities, manage risks and support business continuity.
What are we looking for?
We're looking for someone who combines strong engineering and facilities management experience with genuine leadership ability and a proactive, commercially minded approach.
You'll be comfortable operating at both a strategic and operational level, making decisions, challenging existing practices and balancing reliability, cost, safety and business performance.

job.description:
The Community Safety Officer will lead on complex community safety concerns, high-risk anti-social behaviour, hate incidents, neighbourhood harm, community tension and place-based problems affecting RBH customers and communities. The role focuses on identifying risks, supporting victims, coordinating partnership interventions and delivering sustainable solutions through prevention, support, enforcement and legal remedies where appropriate.
Working closely with customers, neighbourhood colleagues, Greater Manchester Police, Rochdale Borough Council and other partners, the post holder will play a key role in creating safer communities, reducing harm and improving neighbourhood confidence.
Qualifications:
•
English and Maths GCSE Grade 4/C or above (or equivalent)
•
CIH Housing Qualification Level 3 (desirable) or willingness to work towards
•
Relevant qualification or professional training in Community Safety, Housing, or ASB (desirable)
•
Full UK Driving Licence and access to a vehicle for business use
Key Areas of Work:
•
To lead on complex and high-risk anti-social behaviour, hate incidents, harassment and community safety concerns where significant impact,
vulnerability or risk has been identified.
•
To undertake comprehensive risk assessments, vulnerability assessments and support assessments, ensuring the needs of victims, witnesses and affected communities remain central to all interventions.
•
To act as the lead officer for repeat victimisation cases, ensuring victims receive appropriate support, communication, safeguarding and advocacy throughout case management.
•
To identify emerging community safety risks, trends and neighbourhood issues, using data, intelligence and customer feedback to inform targeted interventions and preventative action plans.

To coordinate and deliver neighbourhood problem-solving initiatives that address the root causes of anti-social behaviour and community harm, working collaboratively with customers and partner agencies.

To identify safeguarding concerns involving adults and children and ensure appropriate referrals, interventions and protective actions are implemented.

To coordinate responses to community safety concerns including hate incidents, exploitation, cuckooing, neighbourhood intimidation, criminality affecting communities and other issues impacting customer safety and wellbeing.
•
To support the delivery of mediation, restorative approaches, behaviour change interventions and other early intervention measures designed to prevent escalation of anti-social behaviour.

To contribute to the development of community safety campaigns, engagement initiatives and awareness activities that promote safer neighbourhoods and improve community confidence.
•
To prepare and present reports, case summaries, performance information and intelligence updates to support operational decision-making and service improvement.

Experience of managing complex community safety, anti-social behaviour,

Understanding of prevention, early intervention and restorative approaches to managing anti-social behaviour
